newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 40 billion bolivar ($127 million) auction of 180-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 13.52 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer ten billion bolivars ($42 million) in 269-day bills with a 13.74 percent coupon, and another ten billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 13.97 percent coupon.
Fifty billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 70 billion bolivar issue. Then 180-, 269- and 358-day notes carried 15.20, 15.48, and 15.77 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened between 160 and 183 basis points along the curve to 13.52, 15.06 and 16.04 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
